items.reason: The asynchronous legacy writes inherit request cancellation and can abort when the handler returns.
Storage.Create failures are incorrectly recorded in the legacy duration metric.
Storage.Update failures are incorrectly recorded in the legacy duration metric.
Delete's success metric uses the object name instead of options.Kind, producing per-object label values.
Legacy.DeleteCollection measurements are incorrectly attributed to the storage metric.
The general report of incorrect metric labels encompasses Delete's use of the object name in the kind label.
Delete installs d.Log in the context instead of the enriched per-call logger.
Storage.Create failures and their duration are incorrectly attributed to the legacy metric.
Storage.Update failures are recorded through recordLegacyDuration using the storage start time.
Legacy.DeleteCollection emits a storage duration observation instead of a legacy observation.
The comment explicitly identifies Delete's loss of enriched logging fields by putting d.Log in the context. It additionally describes the metric-label problem in issue #03.
Delete returns on unified-storage NotFound before attempting legacy deletion, preventing deletion of legacy-only objects.
Background legacy writes inherit request cancellation and can terminate before completing; the proposed fix detaches cancellation.
Delete puts object names into the kind metric label, causing per-object cardinality.
Delete propagates d.Log instead of the request-scoped logger containing the added fields.
Storage.Create errors are recorded under the legacy metric instead of the storage metric.
Storage.Update errors and duration are recorded under the legacy metric instead of the storage metric.
The legacy DeleteCollection call is measured with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.
Successful Delete measurements use name instead of options.Kind for the kind label.
The asynchronous legacy Create inherits request cancellation and can abort after unified storage has committed.
The asynchronous legacy Update inherits request cancellation and can leave legacy storage stale.
The asynchronous legacy Delete inherits request cancellation and can leave the legacy object undeleted.
The tests neither wait for nor verify asynchronous legacy writes, so removing those writes would leave the tests passing.
The storage-failure Create test configures its error through setupLegacyFn and only works because both backends share one mock.
